title: Jiaozi: Song government paper money (Chengdu)
summary: In Sichuan, merchant houses issued jiaozi notes against deposits of iron coin. After some issuers went bankrupt, the Northern Song government took over issue: a Paper-Notes Office was founded in 1023 on the proposal of Xue Tian, prefect of Yizhou (centred on Chengdu), and a government series followed in 1024, limited to Sichuan.

uncertainty.note: 1023 is the takeover and the founding of the office; 1024 is the first government series. Sources differ on which year to call the start of state paper money.

as_recorded.value: in 1023 the Song government took over the issue of jiaozi
In 1024, the government itself gave the issuing monopoly

importance.justification: Described by a UCLA historian quoted in one source as the world’s first viable paper currency.

sources.title: The Rise and Demise of Paper Money in Imperial China

reviewer_note: Least sure: the 1023 vs 1024 split. One source says no Song specimens survive. The pin is Chengdu because Planet Banknote calls Yizhou the prefecture centred on Chengdu.
